title: Minimum Window Subsequence
summary: Given strings s1 and s2, identify the shortest continuous segment within s1 where s2 appears as a subsequence.
statement: Given strings s1 and s2, identify the shortest continuous segment within s1 where s2 appears as a subsequence. If no such segment exists, return an empty string. If multiple segments of the same minimum length exist, choose the one starting earliest in s1.
constraints: s1 and s2 are lowercase strings; find a contiguous s1 window containing s2 as a subsequence.
Minimize window length, breaking ties by earliest start; return empty when impossible.
reference_solution:
def minimum_window_subsequence(s1,s2):
    best='';index=0
    while index<len(s1):
        target=0
        while index<len(s1):
            if s1[index]==s2[target]:
                target+=1
                if target==len(s2):break
            index+=1
        if target<len(s2):break
        end=index+1;target-=1
        while target>=0:
            if s1[index]==s2[target]:target-=1
            index-=1
        start=index+1;candidate=s1[start:end]
        if not best or len(candidate)<len(best):best=candidate
        index=start+1
    return best

hints: A forward scan finds a complete subsequence endpoint; a backward scan then contracts that window to its latest possible start.
Repeat forward matching and backward contraction from the next start.
Advance through s1 for s2, retreat through s2 to shrink, record if shorter, then restart just after the contracted start.
Every minimal window has a first complete endpoint found by a forward scan, and backward contraction produces its unique shortest start.
